newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE CLOTHING SOUTH AFRICA-BOUND NEXT WEEK.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE CLOTHING SOUTH AFRICA-BOUND NEXT WEEK.

text.p: Zimbabwe should start exporting clothing and textile products to South Africa from next week under a delayed preferential tariff concluded between the two countries last year, a South African official said on Tuesday night.

Hennie Erasmus, counsellor (economic) at the South African High Commission, said a memorandum of understanding reached last August on the reinstatement of 1964 preferential tariffs on Zimbabwean clothing and textiles was effective from March 1 but some technical difficulties had delayed its implementation.

"We can say that all the technical difficulties we experienced have been ironed out and we expect to see Zimbabwean clothing and textiles in South Africa within the next week or early April," Erasmus told reporters.

He said under the memorandum of understanding, Zimbabwean clothing exports to South Africa would attract 30 percent duty for the next three years which would thereafter be reduced by three percent annually.
He added that further details of the memorandum would be announced on Thursday by Zimbabwe's industry and commerce ministry.

South African High Commissioner Kingsley Mamabolo hailed the implementation of the textiles and clothing memorandum as a major breakthrough in trade negotiations between Harare and Pretoria which have been going on for the past four years.

He and Erasmus said the talks were aimed at reinstating preferential tariffs Zimbabwe enjoyed under a 1964 pact which lapsed in 1992, and South Africa tripled import duties on clothing and textiles to about 90 percent.
They said they expected the trade talks in other sectors such as agriculture and the leather industry to be concluded by June.
"Things are really moving now. We want to be finished with the negotiations before the middle of the year," Erasmus said.
